doc.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: First published review in Moonshadow
summary: His first jazz publication, a review of the 1972 Newport festival in New York.

blocks.x: They hired me off the street as an 18-year-old to come in and do guest lectures at Columbia University. And although they gave me only a little peso or something like that, I was paid. That wouldn’t happen again for twenty years. Not quite that bad. Then there was a magazine, such an obscure publication that if you were to search for it even on the Internet for the rest of your life I’m sure you’ll find no mention of it, called Moonshadow. And I reviewed the Newport Jazz Festival’s first New York — when it came to New York in ’72. And I guess that would be my first formal jazz publication, a little over thirty years ago, and probably the September ’72 issue of Moonshadow if you want to really torture yourself.
I found it. I found it in 1997, almost, over 25 years after its publication. And I was terrified — I always thought if I ever find this again I’m going to realize what a jerk I

was when I was 21. I was 21 when I wrote that review. And it’s a good review. I’m pleased. I give myself — I’m harder on myself. You know since there’s no other comparison that I’m putting on your film’s record. I mean I was ready to tear me to shreds if I’d like took one misstep. And I took no missteps.
